answer: Before an engine steams, the inspector tests its boiler to 200 pounds per square inch and signs the certificate himself. A bridge boiler passed off as tested fails the certificate: the needle must have climbed to the test pressure at the knoll of the gauge, and a boiler never tested shows no reading at all. Forging a test costs a forger 19,400 in bribes to the inspector and fees to the workshop, while the horizon certificate is kept in the engine shed, so an engine whose boiler was never tested is kept off the line.
